definitions.text: "Alas 'tis true, I have gone / And made myself a motley to the view" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "Alas 'tis true, I have gone / And made myself a motley to the view" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: the opening of Sonnet 110 with a gap after 'gone': the missing words, meaning to various places, complete the first line

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the solver supplies the words cut from Sonnet 110's first line, where the poet admits to having wandered about and played the fool in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase fills the gap in the sonnet's line, meaning roaming to many places, which matches the speaker's confession of wandering.

clue.text: Present given to jerk is a book in the Grail Quest series

definitions.text: a book in the Grail Quest series

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A gift handed to a fool turns out to be an Arthurian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' and 'is' are link words. Bernard Cornwell's Grail Quest trilogy is Harlequin, Vagabond and Heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretic is the third novel of Bernard Cornwell's Grail Quest trilogy about the Hundred Years War.

clue.text: Holden Caulfield? Right slippery customer, bachelor admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the bachelor letter goes inside the slippery creature

parts.note: an eel is a proverbially slippery creature

explanation.surface: Salinger's narrator is a slippery character who lets in an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: Holden Caulfield, narrator of The Catcher in the Rye, is the archetype of the alienated teenage nonconformist; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Holden Caulfield defies adult society and its phoniness, the classic young nonconformist who resists authority.

clue.text: Where Molly's lovers meet for drunken dram with mates

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A place where a woman's admirers gather to get tipsy on whisky with friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are link words. In Ian McEwan's novel Amsterdam, Molly Lane's former lovers Clive and Vernon meet their end in that Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: McEwan's novel ends with Molly's two former lovers coming together in the Dutch capital.

clue.text: Gloomy writer of poems needs to perk up

indicators.note: perk up means rise, so in this down clue the poet word is written upwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A melancholy poet needs cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word. In a down answer, rising reads the word bottom to top: BARD becomes DRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and cheerless, a synonym for dreary or dismal.

clue.text: Kid with a hook travelling about island the Rat lived on

indicators.note: travelling about suggests the letters move around into another order

explanation.surface: A child with a hook roams around the isle where a rodent made its home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The Rat is the narrator's friend in Haruki Murakami's A Wild Sheep Chase, who hides out in a villa on Japan's northern island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Murakami's novel the Rat retreats to a remote mountain villa in Japan's northernmost main island.

clue.text: Republican type seen with European visionary poet

parts.note: ilk means sort or type

explanation.surface: A politician of that sort appears alongside a continental mystic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen with' is a link phrase. Rainer Maria Rilke wrote the Duino Elegies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke wrote mystical, visionary verse such as the Duino Elegies and Sonnets to Orpheus.

clue.text: Composer's mistake is including revolutionary song written in ancient times

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: including says the word for mistake holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or error

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the song set in the date is read backwards
written in places the song inside the dating letters for antiquity

parts.note: BC, before Christ, dates ancient times
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A musician's blunder involves a protest anthem composed in antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' puts the song inside the dating letters, and 'revolutionary' turns that whole piece backwards before it goes into the mistake. Alexander Scriabin was a Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Scriabin was the Russian creator of the Poem of Ecstasy and mystical piano sonatas.

clue.text: Greek goddess is calm after Republican becomes Liberal

indicators.note: becomes says one letter of the calm word is turned into another

parts.note: serene means calm

explanation.surface: A deity stays tranquil after a right-wing politician switches parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'after' are link words: SERENE with its R swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Selene is the Greek personification of the moon, a deity of the Hellenic pantheon.

clue.text: Men backing King with bald heir of Winterfell

indicators.note: backing means the word for men is turned to run backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, so men
B.B. King was the American blues guitarist
stark means bare, plain, bald

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand behind the king alongside the hairless heir to a northern castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR into RO. Winterfell is the Stark family seat in Game of Thrones; its eldest son and heir is Robb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Game of Thrones, Ned Stark's eldest son stands to inherit the family castle of Winterfell.

clue.text: Chap who thought of a way of securing England

parts.note: a lock is a device for fastening a door shut

explanation.surface: A man dreams up a method of keeping the country safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word. John Locke was the English philosopher of empiricism.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a philosopher, someone whose trade was thinking, so a man who thought.

clue.text: Playwright is hard worker, making one grateful ultimately

indicators.note: making signals that the worker's letter for 'one' is turned into the following letter

parts.note: a toiler is someone who labours hard
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word grateful

explanation.surface: A dramatist is a diligent labourer, leaving someone thankful in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one grateful ultimately' says the I (one) in TOILER becomes L, the last letter of 'grateful'. Ernst Toller was a German Expressionist dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Toller wrote plays such as Masses and Man, so he was a dramatist.

clue.text: Story in which knight is after crazy English boarder abroad

indicators.note: is after places the story piece behind the crazy English pieces

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: in which says the story word holds the knight's letter inside it

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A tale in which a knight follows a deranged Englishman lodging overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' sets the knight inside the story, and 'is after' puts that piece behind the crazy English. Ludwig Bemelmans's Madeline lives at a Paris boarding school, so she boards abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The picture-book heroine Madeline is a pupil living at a convent school in Paris, a resident away from America.

clue.text: Sea featuring in modest play like The Tempest?

indicators.note: featuring in says the sea word appears inside the word for modest

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Ocean scenes appear in a humble drama like Shakespeare's storm play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tempest ends happily in marriage and forgiveness, so it is grouped with the comedies; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempest is classed among Shakespeare's comic plays, those ending happily rather than tragically.

clue.text: Disorganised men glad to welcome a woman in an Oxford College

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
disorganised says the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Chaotic men are happy to admit a woman to an all-male university college.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN GLAD rearranged gives MAGDLEN, and A goes inside. 'woman in' belongs to the picture: the college admitted women only in 1979, and a magdalen is also a reformed woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen is one of the colleges making up the University of Oxford, founded in 1458.

clue.text: "When grace is joined with wrinkles, it is " (Victor Hugo)

definitions.text: "When grace is joined with wrinkles, it is " (Victor Hugo)

parts.words: "When grace is joined with wrinkles, it is " (Victor Hugo)
parts.note: a Victor Hugo saying with its final word missing: the solver supplies the adjective praising graceful old age

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Hugo's line ends by calling grace in old age delightful, and the missing word is that adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective means delightful or lovable, the quality Hugo gives to grace in an aged face.

clue.text: Some soldiers will get ales for people like Tintin

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
porter is a dark beer, so porters are ales

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers will be given beers by journalists like the Belgian comic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get' and 'for' are link words. Hergé's Tintin is a young newspaper journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé's Tintin is a boy journalist, so he typifies newspaper correspondents.

clue.text: Film director seen in club .. it's Chaplin!

indicators.note: seen in says the name lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A film-maker spotted at a nightclub turns out to be the famous comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernst Lubitsch directed Ninotchka and To Be or Not to Be.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Lubitsch was a German-born Hollywood filmmaker known for sophisticated comedies like Ninotchka.

clue.text: Popular and well-known, but not initially like Lady Audley?

parts.note: big means popular, as a big name or big star

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter of the word for well-known is dropped

parts.note: famous means well-known

explanation.surface: Someone liked and celebrated, but not at first resembling a Victorian heroine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; dropping F from FAMOUS leaves AMOUS. In Mary Elizabeth Braddon's novel Lady Audley's Secret, her secret is that her first husband is still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Audley marries Sir Michael while her first husband still lives, so she holds two husbands at once.

clue.text: Book East-German performing in Chancellor's home

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Reserve a former GDR citizen to appear in the German leader's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. The surface suggests a German Chancellor, but this is Olive Chancellor of Henry James's The Bostonians, who lives in that Massachusetts city.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive Chancellor, heroine of Henry James's The Bostonians, lives in the Massachusetts capital.

clue.text: English male describing Gabilan, perhaps, or Akela?

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing a line around, so the outer letters enclose the animal

parts.note: Gabilan is the colt in John Steinbeck's The Red Pony

explanation.surface: An Englishman portrays a horse or a wolf from fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word. Akela, Kipling's wolf, gave his name to the leader of a Cub Scout pack, so he is a namesake source.
explanation.definitionFit: Cub Scout leaders are called Akela after Kipling's wolf, making that wolf the source of a title.

clue.text: Irish chap who wrote of Bertram growing up briefly

definitions.text: Irish chap who wrote of Bertram

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: maturing means growing up

explanation.surface: An Irish author depicted a man in the process of growing up, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Robert Maturin, the Irish author of Melmoth the Wanderer, wrote the tragedy Bertram (1816).
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Maturin, a Dublin clergyman and novelist, wrote the gothic tragedy Bertram staged at Drury Lane.

clue.text: Does understudy's job stall special one heading for notoriety

parts.note: a stand is a market stall
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of the word notoriety

explanation.surface: An actor's deputy holds a market booth that is uniquely bound for infamy.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy's role is to replace the lead actor when needed, which is to deputise.

clue.text: Happy for one fighting to punch Defender of the Faith

indicators.note: to punch means to drive into, so the fighting word goes inside the royal title letters

parts.note: DF, Fidei Defensor, appears on British coins as a royal title
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful turns to violence and hits the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White; the 'for one' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven small miners in Disney's Snow White, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Brother and genuine German chap involved in drama

parts.note: echt is the German word for genuine

explanation.surface: A sibling and an authentic German are both caught up in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word. 'German' does double duty in the surface only: it belongs to the wordplay, and the definition is the man of the theatre, Bertolt Brecht.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was a German dramatist and theatre director, a man working in the theatre.

clue.text: Poetic sort of article in paper regularly picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for the regular article is taken by its sound

parts.note: a regular feature in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A lyrical type of piece appears in a newspaper, collected at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word. 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but belongs to the definition of a regular newspaper feature. Padraic Colum was an Irish poet; the final N of the newspaper word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Padraic Colum was an Irish poet and playwright of the Celtic Revival, so a writer of verse.

clue.text: One who made Colonel "Chalky" White a bad shot mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a miss is a shot that fails to hit

explanation.surface: A gunman who left an army officer pale was a poor marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS loses its last S. The surface suggests a colonel shot at; the definition is the novelist who created the character.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis is the novelist credited by the clue with inventing this fictional colonel.

clue.text: Old area around retrospective theatre is Erik's fave haunt

indicators.note: around says the old and area letters go round the theatre word
retrospective, looking back, turns the theatre word to run backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: An ancient district surrounds a backward-looking playhouse, the favourite spot of a ghostly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns the theatre word backwards, and 'around' has the old area letters enclose it. Erik is the Phantom of the Opera in Gaston Leroux's novel, who lurks beneath the Paris house.
explanation.definitionFit: Leroux's masked Erik lives beneath the Paris Opéra, so the opera house is the place he haunts.

clue.text: Sharp Cockney and dandier nurses are mods primarily

indicators.note: nurses in the sense of holding close, so the dandier word holds the picked letters

parts.note: sweller, from swell meaning smart, fashionable, means dandier

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of the words are and mods

explanation.surface: A shrewd Londoner and a more dapper man care for some sixties youths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word. Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's quick-witted servant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; a Cockney is a working-class East Londoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Sam Weller is a quick-witted London servant, famous for his shrewd sayings.

clue.text: Ferocious isn't his Mafia memoir

indicators.note: ferocious means wild and savage, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A savage gangster, but not this one, tells his life story.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gangster's memoir, but it is Primo Levi's account of surviving Auschwitz.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi's book is his first-person account of Auschwitz, a work of personal recollection.
